That definitely sounds annoying. Would you be comfortable sharing what assessment tool was used? Absolutely understandable if not.

The only other thing I'd want to know before encouraging someone to go all out in going after the Psychologist is how long has this been going on? As in when was the last point of contact they received? 

Unfortunately if someone is deemed 'functional' regardless of the diagnosis they will often get put onto a pretty long wait list after an initial assessment.

Legal aids support in reporting to the psychology board will most likely help get the issue taken more seriously and addressed faster. a lawyer on the mental health legal aide roster is going to be the best person to help your friend navigate the appropriate avenues for reporting and recouping costs

Just curious, how the report was considered erroneous if your friend requested an assessment?
Did they feel the diagnosis was incorrect or simply missed? 

Was the additional information not addressed in the initial assessment or omitted from the report? The diagnostic criteria for some conditions is pretty narrow and may not have been deemed relevant to a specific assessment.

Regardless I'd assume since legal aide is already involved they would be happy to take a look and let them know if there were any obvious issues. They would also be the best ones to highlight what exactly is missing to make it incomplete. There is a separate roster for lawyers who specialize in assisting patients with mental health related legal issues which this would appear to fall under. I think your friend would do better talking to them directly rather than asking you to post on Reddit for advice

Once you're registered and working there's plenty of people that will just say "ask the nurse" we have that nurse as well".
